persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Bora Özkent published a members-only video on the US midterms and did not try to predict the outcome. In his view, even if Democrats take both chambers they cannot pass major laws, so indices may generally rise, but individual companies could face investigations and sentiment pressure. The highlighted risks are **Tesla**/SpaceX, crypto firms such as **Bitcoin** and **Coinbase**, banks and AI data centers; on the positive side are health insurers and alternative energy.

Bora Özkent also says Trump could harden on Iran using commander-in-chief powers, no easing in tariffs is expected and budget gridlock may bring frequent shutdowns. He asked viewers not to expect portfolio changes from him and to manage their own risk.

items.title: ABD Seçimlerinde Mavi Dalga: Borsada Hangi Şirketler Riskte?
items.summary: The video covers the sector effects of Democrats taking both the House and Senate. Main thesis: because major legislation becomes harder, indices rise after the election, but committee probes and appointments create company-specific pressure. Elon Musk's companies (SpaceX, Tesla) and banks could suffer from more regulation. Crypto is seen as clearly negative as the Clarity Act would stall and firms like Coinbase could be probed. Health insurers and alternative energy are positive, fossil energy and data centers (energy, water, permits) negative. Tariffs continue, China chip restrictions may increase, the deficit won't close and shutdown risk persists. Housing is weak with record-low existing-home sales and rates not falling. Post-election-morning volatility is possible but should calm; he says not to expect portfolio changes from him.

assets.note: Expects a sharp pullback if Democrats win because of the Elon Musk link.
Clarity Act gets blocked and crypto firms face probes.
Sees crypto as 'certain to be negatively affected'.

persons.name: Defiant Gatekeeper
persons.digest:
According to Defiant Gatekeeper the market's patience is running out: big tech reported cloud growth but was punished for rising capex and negative free cash flow. **Alphabet**, **Meta**, **Intel** and **Amazon** fell while only **Microsoft** rose because it spent less capex than expected. With the 10-year near 5%, the market wants returns on spending much faster.

On the Fed, rates were held at 3.75-4% on a 10-2 vote with two dissenters wanting a hike, yet the market cut December hike odds. He also flagged Anthropic's S-1 filing and Blackstone's expected BB rating as a sharp risk. Next week **Apple**, **Palantir**, **AMD** and **Qualcomm** will be judged on cash and guidance.

items.title: Market is getting impatient
items.summary: The video focuses on three points: the market punishes cash outflows, the Fed is hawkish but the market doesn't believe it, and Anthropic's IPO nears its target. Weekly moves: S&P 500 -0.6%, Nasdaq -2%, semiconductor index -7.2% in one day on Friday. Cloud growth is strong (Azure 48%, Amazon 39%, Google Cloud 103%) but Google's free cash flow is about -$9B, Meta's 2026 capex rose to $145B, and Amazon's trailing-12-month free cash flow is about -$42B. Intel said 2027 free cash flow will be negative and Q4 revenue $15-16B versus $17B expected. The Fed held 10-2; Logan said at least two more 25bp hikes, Musalem said urgent tightening, and December hike odds fell from 84% to 72%. Anthropic's first-half revenue is about $16.3B, target valuation $1.5-2T, 22 banks are involved; Blackstone expects a BB rating. Apple, Palantir, AMD and Qualcomm earnings are watched next week.

assets.note: Capex raised to $145B, quarterly free cash flow -$2B.
